_note: Cycle I only: rooms for /cycle-i/in-your-space/. Every room describes its wall in centimetres: u runs along the wall, v is height above the floor. A 'frontal' wall is seen straight on (x = u * px_per_cm, y = floor_y - v * px_per_cm), measured from the furniture (seat ~45 cm, desk ~75 cm). A 'camera' wall is seen at an angle: f, cx, cy (pixels), theta_deg (angle between wall and image plane), corner_x / corner_z (cm, the wall's left floor corner relative to the camera) and eye_cm (camera height), fitted to the skirting and ceiling lines with a 260 cm ceiling (living room) or a 55 cm bedside table (bedroom). Hallway scale comes from its door casing (about 210 cm). Pieces hang centred 147 cm above the floor at centre_u, raised to v_range[0] if they would meet the furniture; sizes that leave u_range or v_range are disabled. Then run: python tools/render_rooms.py Wall shades: each room has a hand-checked wall mask (rooms/<id>-wall.png, made with tools/build_wall_masks.py); the viewer scales the wall's own pixels by shade / mean wall colour, so its light and shadow are kept and the artwork is never recoloured.
